19.history: The royal seat and the temple of Macha saw the whole age begin and end in its council chamber. Its lamps were lit late and few in the first year and the lamp-houses let a hundred and forty-three of them go dark in the second. Cathal was crowned there by Macha's rite in {{year:VI-0006}}, the grey mare pulling at her rope at the temple steps, and the mint cut new dies inked with coal until the plain seal of {{year:VI-0050}}. The proclamation of Linn an Dubhain was pinned to its market posts. Buses and hired cars came to its bridge, and the town called them by the humans' names. In the drill hall the rolls of Buidhnean an Dealachaidh were read out, dead towns struck through; in the council chamber Athchuinge Dheireannach an Tionail was received. The regiments went west from it, its lamp-houses were rationed in the war, and the passes of the northern office were printed there. Comhairle na Rìoghachd seated Somhairle mac Lachlainn, fixed the market-due, held over Tagradh na h-Èirig, and in the present year granted Dubhan's Cairt na h-Às-mhalairt at the third hearing. The last coal of Slighe a' Ghuail came into its goods-yard behind carters' horses.
19.known_for: the council, the crowning, and Cairt na h-Às-mhalairt

22.history: The harbour town of Còmhrag Ceann leathan holds the annual melee on its field. In the dry first year the field was worn to dust and the gate took less than in any year its book remembers. From the seventeenth year the gate was paid wholly in coin of the plain seal. After the war the fair-wardens counted more fighters from the middle country than ever before and none from the western hills; fighters of the regiments were entered in {{year:VI-0146}} and An naoidheamh rèisimeid's man won it; and in the present year, fought with staves and fists, one man died, and in an added bout a hewer's son of Cnoc bheag beat An naoidheamh rèisimeid's man in the third exchange.
22.known_for: Còmhrag Ceann leathan, the annual melee
